cues.en: I've been in the entertainment industry for over thirty years.
cues.zh: 我在娱乐行业干了三十多年。

cues.en: I was a very light drinker in my twenties.
cues.zh: 二十多岁时，我酒喝得很少。

cues.en: In my thirties, I was a social drinker.
cues.zh: 三十多岁时，我是社交型饮酒者。

cues.en: And somewhere in my early forties, developed alcohol use disorder,
cues.zh: 到了四十出头，我患上了酒精使用障碍，

cues.en: which is abbreviated AUD.
cues.zh: 简称 AUD。

cues.en: We don't really use the term alcoholism
cues.zh: 我们现在其实不太用“酗酒”这个词了

cues.en: that much anymore because it's too narrow of a term.
cues.zh: 因为它太狭隘了。

cues.en: AUD covers everything from the occasional binge drinker to the chronic daily drinker.
cues.zh: AUD 涵盖了从偶尔暴饮到每天长期饮酒的所有情况。

cues.en: I started to realize that something was very wrong with me when I was always the last person standing at the bar, or at dinner parties when everybody else had switched to coffee, I was still quaffing wine.
cues.zh: 我开始意识到自己问题很大，是因为我总是酒吧里最后还站着的人；或者在晚宴上，别人都改喝咖啡了，我还在畅饮葡萄酒。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: I realized then that I definitely had a problem, so I decided that I would just go cold turkey,
cues.zh: 我意识到自己肯定有问题，于是决定直接彻底戒断，

cues.en: sober,
cues.zh: 滴酒不沾，

cues.en: and I did.
cues.zh: 我做到了。

cues.en: But what I didn't realize is that could cause what's called the alcohol deprivation effect,
cues.zh: 但我没意识到，这会引发所谓的酒精剥夺效应，

cues.en: where once the honeymoon period of sobriety wears off, you're left with
cues.zh: 一旦戒酒后的蜜月期过去，你剩下的就是

cues.en: constant physical cravings for alcohol.
cues.zh: 身体对酒精持续的强烈渴求。

cues.en: So think about it, you drive by a liquor store and you're triggered, you want a drink.
cues.zh: 所以想想看，你开车经过酒类商店，就会受到刺激，想来一杯。

cues.en: You walk by a pub and you get angry because you can't go in there and have just one drink.
cues.zh: 你走过一家酒吧，会感到生气，因为你不能进去只喝一杯。

cues.en: You start isolating from your friends and families because they drink.
cues.zh: 你开始疏远朋友和家人，因为他们喝酒。

cues.en: Developing AUD was an incredibly confusing thing for somebody who admittedly likes to be in control.
cues.zh: 对一个自认喜欢掌控局面的人来说，患上 AUD 是件极其令人困惑的事。

cues.en: I was definitely not in control of this at all.
cues.zh: 我根本控制不了这件事。

cues.en: In fact, I was swept up in a nearly decade long battle with something I refer to as the monster.
cues.zh: 事实上，我曾卷入一场近十年的斗争，对手是我称之为“怪物”的东西。

cues.en: Addiction is a monster,
cues.zh: 成瘾是个怪物，

cues.en: and it affects every ethnicity, social class, race, sex, age, it doesn't matter. You can be the most disciplined person in the world.
cues.zh: 它不分族裔、社会阶层、种族、性别、年龄，这些都无所谓。你可能是世上最自律的人。

cues.en: When it gets you,
cues.zh: 一旦它抓住你，

cues.en: it has you.
cues.zh: 它就把你攥住了。

cues.en: It is in control.
cues.zh: 它掌控着一切。

cues.en: When I finally realized that I was not in the driver's seat monster was, I sought out every single treatment I could possibly find or afford.
cues.zh: 当我终于意识到坐在驾驶座上的不是我，而是怪物时，我寻遍了所有能找到或负担得起的治疗方法。

cues.en: I went to rehab for $30,000
cues.zh: 我去了收费3万美元的戒毒康复中心，

cues.en: to basically drink wheatgrass and do Tai Chi.
cues.zh: 结果基本上就是喝小麦草汁、打太极。

cues.en: I went to talk therapy for over two and a half years for $200 a session. I actually sought out a hypnotherapist who claimed that he had cured a member of the Grateful Dead. That was $400
cues.zh: 我做了两年半多的谈话治疗，每次200美元。我还专门找过一位催眠治疗师，他声称治好过 Grateful Dead 乐队的一名成员。那次是400美元

cues.en: an hour. I went to 12 different meetings
cues.zh: 每小时。我参加了12个不同的

cues.en: of AA in two different countries, I went macrobiotic,
cues.zh: AA 聚会，分布在两个国家；我还试过长寿饮食法，

cues.en: I got my chakras realigned,
cues.zh: 我做了脉轮调整，

cues.en: I tried veganism,
cues.zh: 我试过纯素食主义，

cues.en: you name it, I tried it, and I
cues.zh: 你能想到的，我都试过，而且我

cues.en: prayed.
cues.zh: 祈祷了。

cues.en: Okay? I prayed until my knees were black and blue,
cues.zh: 好吗？我祈祷到膝盖青一块紫一块，

cues.en: and I still kept relapsing
cues.zh: 可我还是不断复发，

cues.en: time and time again. I mean, I think that in the years that I was suffering from AUD and really battling it, I probably relapsed
cues.zh: 一次又一次。我是说，我觉得在饱受 AUD 折磨、真正与它抗争的那些年里，我大概复发了

cues.en: close to 20 times,
cues.zh: 接近20次，

cues.en: And each relapse
cues.zh: 而每次复发

cues.en: became more difficult to recover from.
cues.zh: 都变得更难恢复。

cues.en: They got worse and worse and worse. And here's the thing,
cues.zh: 它们一次比一次糟。而关键是，

cues.en: I wasn't drinking because I had a crummy childhood or because I was suffering from any personal trauma.
cues.zh: 我喝酒并不是因为童年很糟，也不是因为我遭受了什么个人创伤。

cues.en: I mean, if you look at it from the outside, I had a great life. I was in my chosen career.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，从外表看，我的人生很美好。我从事着自己选择的职业。

cues.en: I had a beautiful home. I had friends and family who loved me and supported me.
cues.zh: 我有漂亮的家。有爱我和支持我的朋友和家人。

cues.en: I was drinking because I was physically addicted to alcohol.
cues.zh: 我喝酒是因为我在生理上对酒精上瘾了。

cues.en: That's it.
cues.zh: 就这样。

cues.en: Once I started, I could not stop drinking.
cues.zh: 一旦开始喝，我就停不下来。

cues.en: I have addiction on both sides of my family, and the genetic predisposition
cues.zh: 我家族双方都有成瘾史，而这种遗传倾向

cues.en: coupled with engaging in the behavior, which for me is drinking,
cues.zh: 加上我自己的行为，对我来说就是喝酒，

cues.en: made me an addict.
cues.zh: 让我成了瘾君子。

cues.en: I knew one thing for sure after trying all of these treatments,
cues.zh: 试过所有这些疗法之后，我确信了一件事，

cues.en: and this became very clear.
cues.zh: 这一点变得非常清楚。

cues.en: Doing equine therapy
cues.zh: 做马术疗法，

cues.en: or tai chi in some swanky beachfront expensive rehabilitation
cues.zh: 或者在海滨豪华昂贵的康复中心

cues.en: facility
cues.zh: 打太极，

cues.en: was not going to fix my biological addiction.
cues.zh: 都治不好我生理上的成瘾。

cues.en: By the end of two thousand eight, I had six months of sobriety under my belt,
cues.zh: 到2008年底，我已经戒酒六个月了，

cues.en: and that's when the addict started to talk to me in my head. That's the insidious thing about addiction, is once you have a little bit of sobriety under your belt, you go, hey, I'm not an addict.
cues.zh: 就在那时，我脑子里的瘾开始跟我说话。成瘾最阴险的地方就在于，一旦你戒了一段时间，你就想，嘿，我不是瘾君子。

cues.en: It whispers to you, go ahead,
cues.zh: 它悄悄对你说，去吧，

cues.en: have a drink, you'll be able to control it, just one drink.
cues.zh: 喝一杯，你能控制住的，就一杯。

cues.en: So I listened to that idiot in my head,
cues.zh: 于是我听了脑子里那个傻瓜的话，

cues.en: and I went out to dinner that night, and I had a glass of wine, I came home, and I was so chuffed. Wow, look, the idiot's right, I'm not an addict. I only had one glass.
cues.zh: 那晚出去吃饭，我喝了一杯葡萄酒，回到家，我特别得意。哇，看吧，傻瓜说得对，我不是瘾君子。我只喝了一杯。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 对吧。

cues.en: Day two, I had two glasses. Day three, I had three glasses, plus I picked up a bottle to bring home and drink on the way home. Day five, I was in a full blown binge.
cues.zh: 第二天，我喝了两杯。第三天，我喝了三杯，还买了一瓶带回家，路上就喝。第五天，我已经彻底狂饮了。

cues.en: I was drinking anything and everything. I would have probably drunk vanilla extract if I had it.
cues.zh: 我什么都喝，什么都来者不拒。要是有香草精，我估计连那玩意儿都能喝下去。

cues.en: When I was finally too ill to drink one more drop of alcohol,
cues.zh: 等到我终于病得连一滴酒都喝不下去的时候，

cues.en: I did what I always did,
cues.zh: 我做了我一贯会做的事，

cues.en: went cold turkey and tried to detox.
cues.zh: 直接硬戒，试着排毒。

cues.en: This time, something went very wrong.
cues.zh: 这一次，出了大问题。

cues.en: I started to suffer from seizures in my body.
cues.zh: 我开始出现癫痫发作。

cues.en: I lost all control of my motor controls.
cues.zh: 我完全失去了对运动功能的控制。

cues.en: I couldn't stand up, I couldn't get dressed.
cues.zh: 我站不起来，也没法穿衣服。

cues.en: So I called a friend, and she took me to my one and only medical detox,
cues.zh: 于是我打电话给一个朋友，她带我去了我这辈子唯一一次医疗排毒，

cues.en: where I got to tell you, was not treated very well. In fact, until they had my $3,000,
cues.zh: 我得说，在那儿我受到的待遇并不好。事实上，直到他们拿到我那3000美元，

cues.en: they finally gave me my medication that I needed to stop shaking.
cues.zh: 才终于给了我需要的药物，让我停止发抖。

cues.en: At that point, I felt so humiliated,
cues.zh: 那一刻，我感到无比屈辱，

cues.en: and so down, and so embarrassed by the whole experience
cues.zh: 无比低落，整个经历让我无比难堪，

cues.en: that I checked myself out and I left.
cues.zh: 于是我自行结账离开了。

cues.en: On the way out, there was this little stack of flyers for all these different various treatments for AUD. One of them was for a shot, and this shot promised to eliminate all cravings for alcohol.
cues.zh: 出来的时候，有一小叠传单，宣传各种治疗AUD的不同方法。其中一张是关于一种注射剂，号称能消除所有对酒精的渴望。

cues.en: The shot was over $1,000
cues.zh: 这种注射剂要一千多美元

cues.en: a month.
cues.zh: 一个月。

cues.en: Yet at this point, I would have sold my soul to get better.
cues.zh: 可到了这个地步，为了好起来，我什么都愿意卖。

cues.en: When I got home,
cues.zh: 回到家后，

cues.en: I googled that shot,
cues.zh: 我谷歌了那种注射剂，

cues.en: and it turns out that the main ingredient in it is naltrexone,
cues.zh: 结果发现它的主要成分是纳曲酮，

cues.en: an FDA approved,
cues.zh: 一种FDA批准的、

cues.en: non addictive,
cues.zh: 不会成瘾的、

cues.en: safe medication that's been used to treat AUD since 1994.
cues.zh: 安全的药物，自1994年起就被用于治疗AUD。

cues.en: As I was searching, a book popped up, the rather boldly named The Cure for Alcoholism
cues.zh: 我搜索的时候，跳出来一本书，书名相当大胆，叫《酗酒的解药》

cues.en: by Doctor. Roy Escapa.
cues.zh: 作者是Roy Escapa医生。

cues.en: There was this little sample chapter there, so I read the chapter, and I was absolutely
cues.zh: 当时有一小段样章，我就读了那一章，然后我完全

cues.en: hooked.
cues.zh: 着迷了。

cues.en: This made complete sense to the science lover in my head.
cues.zh: 这对我内心那个热爱科学的人来说完全说得通。

cues.en: It described a treatment called the Sinclair Method, or TSM,
cues.zh: 它描述了一种叫 Sinclair 方法，简称 TSM 的疗法，

cues.en: where one takes an opiate blocker,
cues.zh: 就是服用一种阿片类阻断剂，

cues.en: you wait for an hour so the medication can get into your bloodstream and brain,
cues.zh: 等一个小时让药物进入血液和大脑，

cues.en: and then you drink alcohol.
cues.zh: 然后再喝酒。

cues.en: Sounds counterintuitive,
cues.zh: 听起来很反直觉，

cues.en: I know, but hear me out. Usually,
cues.zh: 我知道，但听我说完。通常，

cues.en: when an addict drinks,
cues.zh: 当成瘾者喝酒时，

cues.en: they get a huge reward from alcohol,
cues.zh: 他们会从酒精中获得巨大的奖励，

cues.en: and that's what makes them want more and more and more.
cues.zh: 这就是让他们想要越来越多、越来越多的原因。

cues.en: But if you drink on an opiate blocker like naltrexone
cues.zh: 但如果你在服用阿片类阻断剂如纳曲酮的情况下喝酒，

cues.en: or nalmefene if you're here in The UK,
cues.zh: 如果你在英国的话，就是纳美芬，

cues.en: instead of the alcohol reinforcing
cues.zh: 那么酒精就不会强化

cues.en: the addictive synapses in the brain,
cues.zh: 大脑中的成瘾突触，

cues.en: the opiate blocker blocks
cues.zh: 阿片类阻断剂会阻止

cues.en: the endorphins from activating the part of the brain responsible for addiction.
cues.zh: 内啡肽激活大脑中负责成瘾的部分。

cues.en: It's as if you have a huge room of endorphins living in your brain. Right?
cues.zh: 就好像你大脑里住着一大群内啡肽。对吧？

cues.en: And every time you drink alcohol, those endorphins rush through the door and they raise hell on your brain and your neural pathways.
cues.zh: 每次你喝酒，那些内啡肽就冲出门，在你的大脑和神经通路上大闹一场。

cues.en: The opiate blocker stops those endorphins
cues.zh: 阿片类阻断剂阻止那些内啡肽

cues.en: from even leaving the room. It slams that door and it locks it, so they can't even get out and play.
cues.zh: 离开那个房间。它砰地关上门并锁上，让它们根本出不来玩。

cues.en: Over the course of a couple days or weeks for some people,
cues.zh: 经过几天或几周的时间，对某些人来说，

cues.en: the body is slowly detoxed,
cues.zh: 身体慢慢排毒，

cues.en: drinking levels dramatically decrease
cues.zh: 饮酒量急剧下降，

cues.en: because your cravings for alcohol
cues.zh: 因为你对酒精的渴望

cues.en: subside.
cues.zh: 消退了。

cues.en: I didn't have a doctor that would prescribe me Naltrexone back then. In fact, when I mentioned it to anybody, they said, what?
cues.zh: 那时候我没有医生愿意给我开纳曲酮。事实上，当我向任何人提起时，他们都说，什么？

cues.en: So I ordered my pills from an Indian pharmacy online,
cues.zh: 于是我在一家印度网上药房订了药，

cues.en: fifty milligrams of hope.
cues.zh: 五十毫克的希望。

cues.en: Took a couple of weeks for the pills to come to me, and when they did, I got to tell you, I was scared out of my mind because
cues.zh: 药片过了几周才寄到，收到的时候，说实话，我吓得要命，因为

cues.en: I thought,
cues.zh: 我想，

cues.en: what if it doesn't work?
cues.zh: 万一没用呢？

cues.en: What if it makes me relapse again? What if it's a worse relapse than the last one?
cues.zh: 万一让我又复饮呢？万一比上次复饮还糟呢？

cues.en: But at this point, I was so desperate,
cues.zh: 但那时我已经绝望到极点，

cues.en: I took my chance.
cues.zh: 我冒险试了一把。

cues.en: So I took the pill,
cues.zh: 于是我吃下药片，

cues.en: I waited the hour,
cues.zh: 等满一个小时，

cues.en: I poured myself a glass of wine,
cues.zh: 给自己倒了一杯葡萄酒，

cues.en: and it was a miracle.
cues.zh: 然后奇迹发生了。

cues.en: I mean, the wine just sat there while I ate my dinner.
cues.zh: 我是说，我吃晚饭的时候，那杯酒就一直搁在那儿。

cues.en: There was no head games, no compulsion, no I want more, more, more, nothing. I took a couple of sips and I went,
cues.zh: 没有心理拉扯，没有强迫感，没有“我想要更多、更多、更多”，什么都没有。我抿了几口，然后觉得，

cues.en: Meh,
cues.zh: 也就那样，

cues.en: I'm done. It
cues.zh: 我不喝了。这

cues.en: was a complete miracle.
cues.zh: 完全是奇迹。

cues.en: Three months into TSM, I had my true moment.
cues.zh: 开始TSM三个月后，我迎来了真正属于我的时刻。

cues.en: There was this billboard
cues.zh: 有一块广告牌

cues.en: I hate this billboard
cues.zh: 我讨厌那块广告牌

cues.en: near where I lived in Los Angeles, and every time I drove by it, it had a huge glass of red wine on it, which was my particular poison, massive glass of red wine, every time I drove by that billboard,
cues.zh: 就在我洛杉矶住处附近，每次开车经过，上面都印着一大杯红葡萄酒，而那正是我的“毒药”，超大一杯红葡萄酒，每次我开车经过那块广告牌，

cues.en: it would trigger me. If I was in drink mode, it would trigger me, I'd go, I want more. If I was in sober mode, I would drive by that billboard and I'd go,
cues.zh: 它都会触发我。如果我在喝酒模式，它就会勾我，我会想，我想要更多。如果我在清醒模式，我开车经过那块广告牌时就会想，

cues.en: damn it, I can't have a glass of wine.
cues.zh: 该死，我不能喝一杯葡萄酒。

cues.en: This particular day,
cues.zh: 但就在那一天，

cues.en: I drove by that billboard,
cues.zh: 我开车经过那块广告牌，

cues.en: and my brain said to me,
cues.zh: 我的大脑对我说，

cues.en: that's just a billboard.
cues.zh: 那只是一块广告牌。

cues.en: I can't even explain to you what a profound moment this was
cues.zh: 我都没法跟你解释，那一刻有多么深刻，

cues.en: because it meant that my thought processes
cues.zh: 因为这意味着，我的思维过程

cues.en: were normal again.
cues.zh: 又恢复正常了。

cues.en: It meant that my brain was fixed.
cues.zh: 这意味着我的大脑恢复正常了。

cues.en: It meant that I was me again.
cues.zh: 这意味着我又做回了自己。

cues.en: Six months into TSM, I was mostly sober,
cues.zh: 采用 TSM 六个月后，我基本上保持了清醒，

cues.en: except for the occasional
cues.zh: 除了偶尔

cues.en: planned drink one hour after taking naltrexone.
cues.zh: 在服用 naltrexone 一小时后有计划地喝上一杯。

cues.en: TSM worked so well for me that I decided to contact Doctor. Roy Escapa and thank him for writing his book.
cues.zh: TSM 对我非常有效，因此我决定联系 Roy Escapa 医生，感谢他写了那本书。

cues.en: I also asked him to thank the American researcher Doctor. David Sinclair,
cues.zh: 我还请他代我感谢美国研究员 David Sinclair 博士，

cues.en: whose life's work,
cues.zh: 正是他毕生的研究成果，

cues.en: quite literally,
cues.zh: 毫不夸张地讲，

cues.en: saved my life.
cues.zh: 拯救了我的生命。

cues.en: I asked him,
cues.zh: 我问他：

cues.en: what can I do to help spread the word about this treatment? He said, well, why don't you write a book? So I did.
cues.zh: “我能做些什么来推广这种疗法？”他说：“那你为什么不写本书呢？”于是我真的写了。

cues.en: That's when my journey of discovery really began.
cues.zh: 我的探索之旅正是由此真正开始。

cues.en: I found out that the World Health Organizations estimate that a person dies...
cues.zh: 我了解到世界卫生组织估计……

cues.en: Three point three million people die every single year
cues.zh: 每年有整整 330 万人

cues.en: from alcohol related causes. That's more than malaria, tuberculosis,
cues.zh: 死于酒精相关的原因。这比疟疾、结核病、

cues.en: AIDS. I also found out that multiple researchers
cues.zh: 艾滋病还要多。我还发现多位研究人员

cues.en: estimate that eighty to ninety percent of people suffering from AUD do not seek treatment,
cues.zh: 估计有 80% 到 90% 患有 AUD 的人并未寻求治疗，

cues.en: and many of these people don't seek treatment because they've been falsely led to believe that they have to give up alcohol for the rest of their lives,
cues.zh: 而其中许多人之所以不求医，是因为被误导，以为必须终生戒酒，

cues.en: which to a 20 or 30 year old can be utterly daunting,
cues.zh: 这对于二三十岁的人来说简直让人望而生畏，

cues.en: not to mention kind of unrealistic.
cues.zh: 更别说还很不切实际了。

cues.en: I also found out that of the ten percent who do seek treatment,
cues.zh: 我还发现，在真正寻求治疗的那 10% 的人中，

cues.en: up to ninety percent of those people are relapsing within the first four years.
cues.zh: 高达 90% 的人会在前四年内复饮。

cues.en: I mean, what other treatable disease can you think of that has this abysmal of a success rate?
cues.zh: 我是说，你能想到还有哪种可治愈的疾病，成功率会如此惨淡？

cues.en: Studies show that tough love and humiliating an addict or making them hit rock bottom is not helping them, it's actually making people worse.
cues.zh: 研究表明，对成瘾者施以严厉的爱、羞辱他们，或让他们跌到谷底，并不能帮到他们，反而会让情况更糟。

cues.en: As doctor Keith Humphries from Stanford University said, it's remarkable that people believe what's needed is more punishment.
cues.zh: 正如斯坦福大学的 Keith Humphries 医生所说，人们竟然相信需要的是更多惩罚，这很不可思议。

cues.en: If punishment worked, there wouldn't be any addiction.
cues.zh: 如果惩罚有效，就不会有人成瘾了。

cues.en: It's a punishing enough experience.
cues.zh: 这本身就是足够惩罚性的经历。

cues.en: He is absolutely
cues.zh: 他绝对

cues.en: right, it is punishing.
cues.zh: 说得对，这确实是一种惩罚。

cues.en: If we addicts had a normal disease, we would be treated with sympathy and comfort.
cues.zh: 如果我们成瘾者得的是一种普通疾病，我们会得到同情和安慰。

cues.en: Instead, we're faced with a barrage of, why can't you just quit?
cues.zh: 相反，我们面对的是一连串质问：你为什么不能直接戒掉？

cues.en: Just say no?
cues.zh: 就直接说不？

cues.en: And a complete lack of understanding or compassion.
cues.zh: 以及完全缺乏理解或同情。

cues.en: Many people suffer for much longer than I did, but the majority of us suffer for about a decade
cues.zh: 许多人遭受的痛苦比我久得多，但我们大多数人会受苦大约十年

cues.en: before finding help.
cues.zh: 才找到帮助。

cues.en: So why do so many people believe
cues.zh: 那么，为什么这么多人相信

cues.en: that a long term battle with alcohol addiction
cues.zh: 与酒精成瘾的长期斗争

cues.en: can be simply stopped
cues.zh: 可以简单地被停止

cues.en: in thirty days or less
cues.zh: 在三十天或更短时间内

cues.en: with nothing but talk therapy and willpower.
cues.zh: 只靠谈话治疗和意志力。

cues.en: It's amazing. It's amazing. The World Health Institute estimates
cues.zh: 太惊人了。太惊人了。世界卫生研究所估计

cues.en: that a person dies every ten seconds from alcohol
cues.zh: 每十秒就有一人死于酒精

cues.en: use disorder.
cues.zh: 使用障碍。

cues.en: Is our current treatment system really the best we can do?
cues.zh: 我们目前的治疗体系真的已经是最好的了吗？

cues.en: The Sinclair Method has a seventy eight percent long term success rate.
cues.zh: Sinclair Method 的长期成功率达到百分之七十八。

cues.en: Imagine a world
cues.zh: 想象一个世界

cues.en: with seventy eight percent less alcohol
cues.zh: 少掉百分之七十八的酒精

cues.en: addicted
cues.zh: 成瘾

cues.en: people.
cues.zh: 者。

cues.en: Imagine the profound impact
cues.zh: 想象一下，那深远的影响

cues.en: that would have on our society.
cues.zh: 会给我们的社会带来什么。

cues.en: Seventy eight percent less broken families,
cues.zh: 破碎家庭减少百分之七十八，

cues.en: less abused children,
cues.zh: 受虐待儿童减少，

cues.en: lost days of work,
cues.zh: 误工天数减少，

cues.en: insurance costs,
cues.zh: 保险成本减少，

cues.en: accidents,
cues.zh: 事故减少，

cues.en: and on and on and on.
cues.zh: 等等，等等，等等。

cues.en: The method uses science
cues.zh: 该方法运用科学

cues.en: to empower your friends,
cues.zh: 来帮助你的朋友、

cues.en: your family,
cues.zh: 你的家人，

cues.en: or even yourself
cues.zh: 甚至你自己

cues.en: to achieve
cues.zh: 实现

cues.en: recovery.
cues.zh: 康复。

cues.en: Thanks to the Sinclair method,
cues.zh: 多亏了Sinclair方法，

cues.en: I was able to control,
cues.zh: 我得以控制、

cues.en: alt, delete
cues.zh: “Alt、Delete”

cues.en: my addiction to alcohol.
cues.zh: 我的酒精成瘾。

cues.en: I am no longer powerless.
cues.zh: 我不再无能为力。

cues.en: The monster is no longer in control.
cues.zh: 那怪物不再掌控我。

cues.en: I am.
cues.zh: 我掌控了。

cues.en: TSM works wonders
cues.zh: TSM对酒精成瘾者

cues.en: for alcohol addicted people.
cues.zh: 效果奇佳。

cues.en: It is my dream to see it become a go to regularly offered treatment for those in need.
cues.zh: 我的梦想是看到它成为一项常规提供的治疗，惠及有需要的人。

cues.en: I encourage all of you, I beg you, to please help spread the word of this life saving treatment,
cues.zh: 我鼓励你们所有人，我恳求你们，请帮忙传播这种救命疗法，

cues.en: and let's give addicts
cues.zh: 让我们给成瘾者

cues.en: the option
cues.zh: 他们应得的

cues.en: they deserve.
cues.zh: 选择。

cues.en: Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢。
